response.title: 300 Petroleum Coke Trucks Stuck at Assam–Bengal Border | Logistics Insider
response.content:
The Andhra Pradesh Lorry Owners’ Association (APLOA) has asked the Union Finance Ministry and the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) to step in over the reported detention of more than 300 trucks at the Assam–West Bengal border. The association says the consignments carry valid GST documents and that Integrated GST (IGST) has been paid on them.

The trucks are carrying raw petroleum coke (RPC), a refinery by-product, from Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) refineries at Bongaigaon, Guwahati and Digboi in Assam. The vehicles have reportedly been held around Srirampur and Bakshirhat since September 17.

Where the cargo is headed

APLOA general secretary Y.V. Eswara Rao said nearly half the trucks were carrying consignments for Visakhapatnam. The rest were bound for Haldia and Durgapur in West Bengal, Barauni in Bihar and Paradip in Odisha.

APLOA wants authorities to verify 16 trucks carrying RPC for Rain CII Carbon (Vizag) Ltd, based on a vehicle list from IOC’s Marketing division, Eastern Region, and to release them if they are being held without lawful grounds. As an example, it cited an e-way bill for truck AP39VW-1447, which records a taxable value of ₹17.28 lakh and IGST of ₹3.11 lakh at 18%. The consignment was invoiced by IOC, Assam, to Rain CII Carbon (Vizag), with Shiva Transport Agency as the transporter.

The cost of standing still

APLOA estimates demurrage and related losses for transporters and other stakeholders at about ₹1 crore. It warns that further delays could disrupt production and raise logistics costs for consignors and consignees.

P. Venkata Siva Nagaraju, a truck owner from Vijayawada, said three of his newly acquired trucks had been held at an outpost on the West Bengal border for more than a month.

The association accepts that valid papers do not exempt cargo from lawful inspection, but says prolonged detention must rest on stated legal grounds. It has sought disclosure of any written orders, better coordination among GST authorities in the states concerned and uniform procedures for vehicles carrying valid documents.

"Orders from above"

Transporters have alleged that police and GST officials on the ground cited only “orders from above” and served no written order. Some transporters have linked the stoppage to West Bengal’s crackdown on illegal coal transport, arguing RPC is a refinery by-product, not mined coal. The Barauni Calciners Association said earlier this month that West Bengal’s commercial taxes commissioner had assured it the matter was resolved, but the trucks were not allowed through. No official explanation from West Bengal authorities has been reported.

The standoff comes as the GST Council has recommended curbs on transit-state checks. Under the proposed changes, goods in transit may be inspected, detained or seized only by officers of the state where the supplier or recipient is located, and not by transit states. Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on October 8 that goods cannot be stopped in between.

With inputs from The Hindu and The Times of India.

Representative image: funky footage / Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.0)

response.title: SOS to PMO after 'orders from above' hold up 300 raw petroleum coke trucks at Assam-Bengal border | Kolkata News - The Times of India
response.content:
KOLKATA: Hundreds of trucks carrying raw petroleum coke from

Indian Oil Corporation

refineries in Assam to calcination units in Barauni, Bihar, have been stranded at the Assam-West Bengal border for more than a fortnight, with authorities in West Bengal allegedly refusing passage without issuing any written order or citing a specific reason.

According to traders and transporters, more than 300 lorries loaded with raw petroleum coke, or RPC, from IOCL refineries at Guwahati, Digboi and Bongaigaon have been stopped around Srirampur and Bakshirhat. The consignments are bound for calcined petroleum coke units in Barauni and other industrial destinations, and are required to pass through West Bengal in transit.

The Barauni Calciners Association has sent an SOS to the Prime Minister’s Office, seeking urgent intervention after representations to the West Bengal Chief Minister’s Office, the Chief Secretary, senior home and finance officials, police authorities and GST officials failed to resolve the matter. The association said the trucks were carrying GST-paid consignments supported by IOCL invoices, e-way bills and other valid documents.

Transporters claimed that police and GST officials on the ground have only referred to “orders from above” while stopping the vehicles. No written communication has been served specifying the issuing authority, legal provision, reason for detention or process for release, they alleged.

Traders said if there was any violation, authorities should inspect the cargo, seize deficient vehicles or issue formal notices, rather than leave hundreds of trucks immobilised indefinitely.

Drivers from several states, including Uttar Pradesh, Punjab and Andhra Pradesh, said they were facing acute hardship due to the prolonged halt. Many reported shortages of food and drinking water, safety concerns at night and instances of diesel theft. Truck owners said they were incurring daily losses and struggling to meet loan instalments as vehicles remained idle.

The Barauni Calciners Association said RPC is a petroleum refinery by-product and distinct from coal. It is the key raw material for calcined petroleum coke, which is used in aluminium smelting and graphite electrode manufacturing. Barauni, in Begusarai district, is a major CPC production hub.

Industry representatives warned that disruption in RPC movement could hit production at CPC units, affect downstream industries and disturb the lifting cycle from Assam refineries. They said every additional day of stoppage was compounding financial losses for manufacturers, traders, transporters and drivers.

The association has urged the Centre to take up the issue with West Bengal at the highest level and ensure immediate movement of all legally documented consignments.
